https://www.iberkshires.com/story/83394/.text: NBCC to Host 14th Annual 'Back-Packed for Success' 08:20AM / Tuesday, July 28, 2026 Print Story | Email Story NORTH ADAMS, Mass. — The Northern Berkshire Community Coalition (nbCC) is hosting its 13th annual back-to-school event for school-aged kids for local Northern Berkshire students entering pre-K through 12th grade. This includes homeschooled students. Students will receive a free backpack to fill with school supplies. The event for families living in Florida and Savoy will be located at Gabriel Abbott Memorial School, 56 North County Road, Florida on Tuesday, Aug. 11 from 5:00p.m. to 6:00pm. Families picking up from Florida and Savoy will receive pre-packed backpacks and will be contacted to choose the color of their child's backpack. The event for families living in Williamstown, North Adams, Clarksburg, Adams, and Cheshire will be located at the St. Elizabeth's of Hungary Parish Center on St. Anthony Drive, North Adams on Thursday, August 13 from 1:00pm to 3:00pm. Families picking up at this location should bring their children to choose their backpacks and school supplies at the event. This event requires pre-registration to ensure there are enough backpacks and supplies ready for each child, as supplies are limited. Families can register online at: https://forms.gle/ rGpoMUE4XbZ9WNiL7 or by contacting nbCC's Family Resource Center at (413) 663-7588 to register. For more information, contact Nancy Kennedy, Northern Berkshire Community Coalition at (413) 663-7588. Tags: NBCC , Greylock Youth SummerFest Come join in on the wealth building fun! August 3-8. No Comments North Adams Becomes a Purple Heart Community By Jack Guerino iBerkshires Staff 05:16AM / Tuesday, August 11, 2026 Veterans Service Officer Kurtis Durocher, a Purple Heart recipient, tells his own story of how he was wounded in Iraq. NORTH ADAMS, Mass. — City leaders last week held a ceremony marking the city as a Purple Heart Community to honor local military service members wounded or killed in combat. "This designation is much more than a sign that will stand at the entrances to our city," said Kurtis Durocher, Northern Berkshire veterans service officer at City Hall on Friday. "It is a lasting commitment and a promise to this community. We'll never forget the sacrifices made by those who are wounded or killed while serving our nation. It is a public declaration of the courage and sacrifices of combat wounded. Veterans will always have a place of honor here in North Adams." As a Purple Heart Community, North Adams will place signs throughout the city acknowledging the designation. The city will also hold a ceremony every Aug. 7 on National Purple Heart Day. During the inaugural ceremony, Durocher said he was asked by the Military Order of the Purple Heart to find a keynote speaker for the event, preferably a Purple Heart recipient. But he was unable to find someone willing to speak. With the date approaching, he decided to tell his own story. "I don't like standing up and telling my own personal story ... But I realized, in my position as a VSO, I get so many ... children of veterans who will say, 'I didn't know anything about my father until after he passed because he just didn't talk about it,'" Durocher said. "... I have been that way until I've gotten into this position, and so, now, I try to tell my story as much as I can when it is brought to me." Durocher served in the Army for 20 years and retired as a master sergeant. On Friday, he recalled a time early in his career while serving in the 82nd Airborne Division deploying to Iraq during Operation Iraqi Freedom. On Sept. 12, 2003, his squad was conducting a patrol on Route Irish in Baghdad. He was serving as a gunner on an LMTV when it was struck by a 155-millimeter artillery shell. He said the explosive had been hidden behind a guardrail and detonated using nothing more than a washing machine timer. "In an instant, everything changed. The blast knocked me unconscious. When I regained consciousness, I instinctively was removing my helmet," he said. "Almost immediately my training took over. We had been taught repeatedly that attacks like this were often followed by a secondary attack or an ambush. I quickly put my helmet back on and began searching for my machine gun." Photograph: Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Donald Trump Donald Trump scolds CNN anchor for covering him at the UN President chided Kaitlan Collins for asking him question at UN after White House ban on CNN, MS Now and Politico Ariana Baio Tue 22 Sep 2026 13.09 EDT Last modified on Tue 22 Sep 2026 14.42 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Donald Trump has scolded a CNN anchor for covering him at the UN in New York after banning the network and two other media outlets from the White House. Kaitlan Collins asked the US president on Tuesday when the Iran war would end, citing a poll that claims two-thirds of Americans don’t think the US is winning. “It’s an honor to be here. I’m surprised that CNN is here covering me,” Trump began before telling Collins: “You should not be here covering me. “You said you weren’t going to cover me. You shouldn’t be covering me.” 0:56 ‘You shouldn’t be here,’ Donald Trump tells CNN at UN general assembly – video Collins told the president on Tuesday that the UN allowed her organization into the general assembly. The Guardian has asked CNN for comment. Last week, Trump announced he was banning CNN, Politico and MS Now from the White House, accusing the outlets – without citing evidence – of “constantly” writing and reporting “FICTION and LIES”. On Saturday, reporters and other staff from the news organizations were denied access to the White House. On Saturday, CNN said: “We will not be deflected from our duty to hold the government and other public bodies to account, and we will continue to report on the actions and processes of this administration without fear or favor.” CNN, Politico and MS Now have since sued the administration, seeking to end his enforcement of the ban and restore reporters’ hard passes that grant them access to the White House grounds. A federal judge is expected to hold a hearing on the matter on Wednesday. Trump’s attempt to restrict press access sparked criticism from other media organizations and first amendment advocacy groups, which have accused the US president of infringing on the right of the free press. Trump has defended his decision, claiming his ban was not “an assault on the Free Press”, but instead designed to address “national security” threats – a claim the US president has recently used to justify building a triumphal arch and a White House ballroom. 10:08 Trump v the media: US networks unite in boycott - The Latest Explore more on these topics Donald Trump Press freedom CNN United Nations MS Now US constitution and civil liberties news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed US news US politics Midterms 2026 World Climate crisis Middle East Ukraine US immigration Soccer Business Environment Tech Science Newsletters The Filter Wellness

https://www.aol.co.uk/articles/nato-scra.text: Adam Toms Updated Wed, September 30, 2026 at 5:54 AM UTC 0 Two F-18s were scrambled (Image: Getty) It comes after multiple occasions when aircraft have been sent up in the sky to safeguard NATO airspace. NATO scrambled jets after a possible Russian threat was detected. The aircraft from Spain's airforce took off as an "aerial target" in Ukraine moved close to the Romanian border. The eastern country's Ministry of National Defence posted on X: "On the night of September 29-30, the radar surveillance system of the Ministry of National Defense detected an aerial target moving east of Izmail, in Ukraine, near the river border with Romania. "Two F-18 aircraft of the Spanish Air and Space Force, currently on Enhanced Air Policing combat duty, took off to monitor the situation. The National Military Command Center notified the General Inspectorate for Emergency Situations regarding the implementation of population alert measures in northern Tulcea County, and a RO-Alert message was issued at 00:35. No incursions into national airspace were detected. The air alert ended at 01:10." It comes after planes were scrambled on the night of September 28-29. A radar surveillance system "detected an aerial target operating north of Isaccea, near the river border with Ukraine". "Two F-18 aircraft of the Spanish Air and Space Force, currently on Enhanced Air Policing combat duty, took off to monitor the situation," officials added. Jets were scrambled three times between August 31 and September 6 in response to Russian military aircraft operating near the Baltic states (Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania), according to data from Lithuania's Defence Ministry. Russia launched a missile and drone attack on Kyiv overnight on September 30, killing at least two people and injuring four others, according to local officials. More than a dozen explosions hit the city just before 3am local time. Moscow has intensified its attacks on Kyiv since August, aiming to exhaust Ukraine's air defences, the Kyiv Independent reports. Yesterday, Russia issued a horror nuclear threat to the UK following the airing of a documentary that depicted how a conflict with Britain could play out. The country's UK embassy said on X: "The embassy added on X: "Those advocating a blockade or strike on Kaliningrad should have no illusions about the consequences. "Any British or NATO military action against Russian territory would be met with all means at Russia's disposal, including nuclear weapons." https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026.text: Jeremy Corbyn and Zarah Sultana founded the leftwing Your Party in 2025. Photograph: PA Images/Alamy View image in fullscreen Jeremy Corbyn and Zarah Sultana founded the leftwing Your Party in 2025. Photograph: PA Images/Alamy UK news Met police investigating row over founding of Your Party Inquiry said to have been launched after force received report ‘relating to alleged unauthorised access of a political party’s database’ Alexandra Topping Political correspondent Fri 16 Oct 2026 13.29 EDT Last modified on Fri 16 Oct 2026 13.31 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Police are carrying out a criminal investigation into a row over the founding of Your Party, which split the leftwing party as it was established last year. A spokesperson for London’s Metropolitan police said they had launched an investigation after they received a report in September 2025 “relating to the alleged unauthorised access of a political party’s database”, the Politico website reported. Your Party was founded in summer 2025 by the former Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn and the former Labour MP Zarah Sultana, both of whom now sit as Your Party MPs in the House of Commons. But relations between the different factions in the party have been strained since its creation in July last year. That September Sultana revealed a new membership portal on X, and encouraged members to become paying members for £55. Corbyn described the site as a “false membership system” and told supporters to ignore an email requesting funds. Sultana said her only aim had been to “safeguard the grassroots involvement that is essential to building this party”, and later accused the party of being run by a “sexist boys’ club” . Officers had now arrested a man on suspicion of an offence under the 1990 Computer Misuse Act, a police spokesperson told Politico. The man was released pending further inquiries and has not been charged. Officers also previously interviewed a woman in her 30s under caution in connection with the same investigation. The spokesperson added: “The investigation continues.” The police spokesperson did not name any political party in their statement, and the spokesperson did not confirm which political party their investigation was related to. Sources told the Guardian that the investigation was linked to the long-running dispute connected to the establishment of Your Party. Neither the man arrested nor the woman interviewed by police are MPs and neither have been charged with an offence. Neither Corbyn nor Sultana were accused of wrongdoing, Politico reported. In January, it emerged that the Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO) advised the party that while it was taking no further action over the Your Party membership portal launch, it may have involved “serious criminal activity” and should be referred to the police. A Your Party spokesperson said: “It would not be appropriate to comment any further about ongoing police investigations.” They also said: “We can reassure our members and supporters that our systems are secure and that this was an isolated incident.” Your Party has struggled to make a widespread national impact since it was founded, while the Green party of England and Wales, rebranded as an eco-socialist party, has seen its membership quadruple. In February, Corbyn won a comprehensive victory to become the de facto leader of the leftwing startup party . He said Your Party would work with the Green party and others to push for a “coordinated left-flank offensive” against Reform and Labour. Sultana was also voted on to the party’s leadership committee under its collective leadership model. Corbyn-backed candidates took 14 of the 24 available places on the party’s central executive committee (CEC). Sultana-backed candidates took seven of the seats and three went to independents. https://www.politico.eu/article/nigeria-.text: Nigeria has become the fifth country to detect the rapidly-spreading Ebola strain, with its first confirmed case in a woman who traveled from Uganda. The patient started showing symptoms on Oct. 7, four days after her arrival in the Western African country. She was later admitted to a private hospital in the capital Abuja, where laboratory testing confirmed the Ebola diagnosis, the country’s health minister and the World Health Organization said Tuesday. She is currently in isolation and receiving medical care. Nigeria’s health ministry and disease agency are working with the WHO and Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention to “contain that infection and prevent its further spread.” Advertisement Advertisement The case underscores the difficulty in stopping the spread of the highly-infectious disease. The Democratic Republic of the Congo, the epicenter of the outbreak, is currently grappling with the fastest-growing and deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country’s history, caused by the Bundibugyo strain for which there are no approved vaccines or treatments. As of Oct. 19, Congo reported 9,552 confirmed cases, including 4,602 related deaths. In Nigeria, where there is a more established private health care market and less reliance on international aid for services, health authorities are working to track down and monitor people who may have been exposed, with 44 close contacts already identified. “There is no need for panic,” the health ministry wrote on social media. “What matters is staying informed, practising good hand hygiene, knowing the symptoms and seeking guidance from public health authorities if you suspect exposure.” The disease has also recently spread to Kenya, in Eastern Africa, with nine confirmed cases all linked to a man who traveled from Congo to Uganda before taking a flight to Kenya. He died at a hospital in Nairobi after testing positive for Ebola on Oct. 5. Jean Kaseya, director-general of Africa CDC, told Devex last week this case illustrated the difficulties in contact tracing. Health authorities were still trying to ascertain who was on his flight, and if they had made onward travel, he said. The WHO has urged “all countries in the region to sustain a high level of readiness as the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continues to evolve.” The U.N. health agency, which first declared the outbreak in Congo on May 15, also advised against any restriction of travel to, or trade with, affected countries.
